source.title: Trend-Smooth: Accelerate Asynchronous SGD by Smoothing Parameters Using Parameter Trends
source.authors: Guoxin Cui; Jia-Feng Guo; Yi-Xing Fan; Yan-Yan Lan; Xue-Qi Cheng

record.tranche_reason: Tests training and test performance on MNIST and CIFAR-10 in asynchronous training, an extension beyond the claim versions’ stated settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label test accuracy and loss for asynchronous methods against SGD on MNIST and CIFAR-10. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, large-batch training, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Adaptive-method results compare Trend-Smooth versions with their original asynchronous counterparts, not directly with SGD.
record.test_reason: The paper cites adaptive optimizers' poorer generalization as background but does not test any listed version. Its experiments compare asynchronous training methods and Trend-Smooth modifications. Adaptive-method experiments compare each optimizer with its Trend-Smooth counterpart, without establishing adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under matched tuning. Batch size is fixed within each dataset.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors additionally conclude that Trend-Smooth improves asynchronous Momentum, RMSProp, and Adam when combined with them. Evidence is limited to moderate networks; effectiveness on larger models is an expectation left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses parameter-history trends to modify asynchronous gradient updates; compares against asynchronous SGD, delay-compensated SGD and single-machine SGD. Experiments use moderate neural networks and natural-label MNIST/CIFAR-10 tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and training method affect the reported performance. The paper says Trend-Smooth is comparable to SGD on both datasets, while other asynchronous methods have lower accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Trend-Smooth achieves higher test accuracy than the tested asynchronous baselines and accuracy close to sequential SGD on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-trend adjustments can improve asynchronous training performance in the tested moderate networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Trend-Smooth produces smoother parameter trajectories and larger parameter changes than other tested asynchronous methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-trend adjustments reduce trajectory fluctuation during asynchronous training.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding Trend-Smooth to asynchronous Momentum, RMSProp, and Adam yields faster loss reduction, lower losses, and higher test accuracies than their original counterparts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trend-Smooth can improve the tested asynchronous optimizers on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

record.problems: Numerical table entries are absent from the supplied text; accuracy comparisons are reported qualitatively. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The authors say experiments focus on moderate neural networks and leave larger models to future work.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width variation beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on the same image task and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language-model comparisons.
Batch-size comparisons at fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects across configurations, training-set sizes, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification is unsupported: a new setting must still measure a listed version. Section II.A attributes the adaptive-generalization claim to prior work. Missing numerical table entries prevent numerical verification but do not change the finding that these experiments test different comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels using the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their test-error effects.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons under the specified tuning conditions, including broader tuning, weight decay, switching, and language-model results.
Large-batch versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons across training-set sizes and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: CIFAR1 trained with Trend-Smooth
rows.operation_detail: Measure parameter-curve fluctuation and parameter value change during training.

conditions.value: 20 randomly selected from the last fully-connected layer

rows.measure: Summed standard error and values changed
rows.baseline: A-SGD and A-SGD-alpha parameter curves: more fluctuated; A-DC: largest fluctuation and low value change
rows.value: Trend-Smooth curves were much smoother than other asynchronous methods, and parameters could change larger; exact indicators not stated.
rows.note: This is a measurement of parameter curves, not magnitude-aware sharpness or a reported train-test gap.
rows.check: Parameter-trajectory fluctuation and endpoint changes do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or its association with generalization gaps.
